last_key_points: Crude repriced lower on ceasefire expectations, with Brent near 94.44 and WTI near 94.98, but both remain headline-sensitive to Hormuz access and Gulf strike risk.
Pakistan became the operative diplomatic hub, with first-round U.S.-Iran talks now centered on Islamabad and weekend timing increasingly cited.
Israel's continued operations in Lebanon emerged as the most immediate threat to ceasefire durability, creating a gap between diplomatic messaging and battlefield reality.
Post-ceasefire Iranian missile and drone activity against Gulf states kept regional air defenses active and prevented a clean de-escalation narrative.
Hormuz shifted from near-total disruption to conditional passage for non-enemy shipping, improving flow optics without restoring full commercial normality.
Confirmed satellite evidence of storage-tank damage at Assaluyeh kept energy-infrastructure risk live even as some viral claims about new Gulf-for-Gulf strikes remained contested.
